transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main thing is I feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. Like I can’t really just sit and idle. With the new setup at work, it’s been harder to cover that up or work around it, so I figured I should come in and talk to someone.
Can you tell me if this feeling of needing to always be moving or busy has been present since you were a child, or is it something that started more recently in your adult life?

No, it’s not new. Looking back, it was there when I was a kid too. In grade school, teachers would say I was bright, but careless, and that I’d talk out of turn or needed reminders to stay on my work. I guess I didn’t really connect it to now until recently.
Do you also notice yourself feeling physically restless, fidgety, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking—in your daily life now?

Yeah, I do notice that. If I have to sit through something slow, like a training video or even a long appointment, I start feeling kind of boxed in. I’ll want to stand up, stretch, shift around, or just do something with my hands. It’s not dramatic, but it’s there.
Do you also find yourself losing track of details, forgetting things, or having trouble staying organized or focused on tasks, even when you're not feeling restless?

Yeah, I do. It’s mostly with longer meetings or when I’m trying to read through a new procedure at work. I’ll start off okay, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes have kept going over the page, or I’ve been sitting there listening, but I didn’t really take in what was said. Then I have to go back and try to catch up.
